newsitem.title: GERMANY: Lamfalussy says sure ECB can resist pressure.
newsitem.headline: Lamfalussy says sure ECB can resist pressure.

text.p: European Monetary Institute President Alexandre Lamfalussy was quoted on Monday as saying he was sure the European Central Bank (ECB) could resist political pressure and dismissed as unacceptable any attempt to influence it.
Asked to comment on a French proposal to set up a so-called stability council to act as a counterweight to the ECB, Lamfalussy told Sueddeutsche Zeitung in an interview:
"If the purpose of a stability council should be to influence the central bank council, then that would be unacceptable."
But he added there were many practical issues on which an exchange of opinion was needed between governments and the ECB.

One such issue was exchange rate policy between the euro currency area and the rest of the world. "The Treaty is clear on this in any case -- responsibility for the exchange rate regime lies with the government."
On the other hand central banks could not be instructed to intervene in currency markets to such an extent that it may prove inflationary, Lamfalussy said.
He added that responsibility for a currency's stability did not just lie with a central bank. "It depends much more on the right mixture of monetary and fiscal policy, the policy-mix."

Lamfalussy also said countries seeking to qualify for European Economic and Monetary Union (EMU) would be judged not only on whether they reduced their budget deficits below the reference ratio of three percent of gross domestic product (GDP), one of the criteria for participation, but on how they achieved it.
"That is not clear yet. It could well be that we will find that the planned budget consolidation is not credible."
Cutting the deficit by raising taxes would not be good enough.

"A government should rather cut spending. If it does we must then see where it cuts spending. One can make cuts across the board, or one can make targeted cuts with a lasting impact, like in the pension system, the health system or welfare.

"All governments maintain they are solving the problems. Sustainability is an essential precondition for qualifying for monetary union," Lamfalussy said, adding that countries' budget plans for 1998 would also be reviewed.
